roles.title: Incident coordinator
roles.summary: Declares the incident, walks the triage tree, assigns the other roles, keeps the clock, and decides when normal service may take over again.
checklist: Write down the time the incident was declared.
Walk the triage tree aloud with at least one other person.
Assign a key custodian, a mirror operator, a verifier, and a scribe. One person may hold two roles, but the verifier never checks their own copy.
Stop any step a checklist marks unsafe until the verifier agrees.
Declare recovery only after the verifier's checks pass, and hand the scribe the time.

roles.title: Key custodian
roles.summary: Holds offline recovery keys and backup passphrases, and signs key rotations. Never types a recovery key into a shared or unverified machine.
checklist: Bring your recovery key and your paper copy of the pinned public keys.
Check the rotation statement's revoked and successor keys against paper before signing.
Refuse any request to lower the recovery threshold during the incident.
Sign only on a machine that verified the bootstrap kit.
Return recovery keys to separate physical storage afterwards.

roles.title: Mirror operator
roles.summary: Stands up emergency mirrors, writes and imports removable media, and restores origins and nodes.
checklist: Never delete or force-push refs on a surviving copy.
Keep every copy you start from untouched until recovery is declared.
Serve emergency mirrors read-only unless the coordinator approves writes.
Record every command you ran and when it finished for the scribe.

roles.title: Verifier
roles.summary: Independently checks signatures, digests, and refs against pinned keys and signed pins. Must not be the person who produced the copy being checked.
checklist: Read pinned public keys from paper, never from the media being checked.
Verify the bootstrap kit before anyone runs a tool from it.
Check restored refs against a signed export or a second independent copy.
Run git fsck on every restored repository.
Say out loud which checks passed and which were skipped.

roles.title: Scribe
roles.summary: Records the exercise or incident: times, missing prerequisites, data loss, unsafe steps, and a corrective owner for every finding.
checklist: Record declared, recovered, and verified times.
List every prerequisite that was missing and who will fix it.
List commits, refs, issues, or pull requests that were lost.
List every unsafe step, whether it was taken or refused.
Give every finding a corrective owner before the debrief ends.

prerequisites.title: A printed or offline copy of this runbook, with the kit digest written on it
prerequisites.check: Two people can find a copy without a network connection.

prerequisites.title: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media
prerequisites.check: kit verify passes against the kit key written on paper, before the review date.

prerequisites.title: Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people
prerequisites.check: The keys on paper match roster check output.

prerequisites.title: Enough recovery key custodians, in separate places, to meet the roster threshold
prerequisites.check: roster check reports the threshold is met by distinct holders.

prerequisites.title: A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS
At least two copies of each repository under separate control
prerequisites.check: A mirror and a verified removable-media export, or two mirrors run by different people.

prerequisites.title: A backup or export verified within the review interval
prerequisites.check: forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify or forkmesh-mirror-node --restore-drill passed recently.

prerequisites.title: Node backup passphrases stored away from the node
prerequisites.check: The custodian can produce the passphrase file without the node.

prerequisites.title: Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region
Blank removable media large enough for every repository
prerequisites.check: The media is labelled and stored with the kit.

prerequisites.title: A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet
prerequisites.check: Two machines can reach each other by address.

steps.action: Copy the kit from removable media to a local directory. Do not run anything from it yet.
Verify the kit with the kit public key written on paper.
steps.expect: Exit 0 and the manifest digest you wrote on the printed runbook.
steps.unsafe: Never take the trusted key from the kit itself; a forged kit carries its own key.

steps.action: If verification exits 4 (stale), continue, but give the scribe a finding to rebuild the kit.

verify.check: kit verify exits 0 or 4 with the pinned kit key.
The printed manifest digest matches the digest the tool prints.

rollback.action: Discard the copy and verify the second custodian's kit instead.

procedures.title: Find mirrors and contacts without the website

steps.action: Check the roster from the verified kit and list its mirrors, addresses, and contacts.
steps.expect: Exit 0, the active keys, and every mirror address.

steps.action: Try each mirror address, starting with the ones that need no DNS.
Reach roster contacts over the channels the roster lists: phone, radio, or in person.

verify.check: At least one mirror answered, or every contact was tried and the answers are written down.

rollback.action: Nothing to undo: discovery only reads.

steps.action: List the refs of every mirror, clone, and export people still hold.
Verify each removable-media export against the pinned export keys.
For each ref, find the most advanced copy: the one whose tip contains every other copy's tip.

verify.check: Every ref has one chosen source, and diverged refs are written down rather than chosen.

rollback.action: Nothing to undo: the inventory only reads.

procedures.title: Restore an origin from surviving copies

steps.action: Create the new origin from the verified surviving mirror.
Push newer work from each local clone. Git refuses anything that is not a fast-forward.
steps.unsafe: Never add --force. A rejected push means the copies diverged; keep both and review.

verify.check: Connectivity check passes.
Every ref in the newest signed export is present, or contained in the restored ref.
Collaboration records under .forkmesh/ are present on their branches.

rollback.action: Delete the new origin directory. The surviving copies were never changed.

procedures.title: Serve a read-only emergency mirror from plain files

steps.action: Copy a verified repository into a directory to serve.
Write the files a static HTTP clone needs.
Serve the directory on the local network.
steps.unsafe: A static mirror has no access control. Serve only public repositories, and only on networks the coordinator approves.

verify.check: A second machine clones the mirror.
The clone's refs match a signed export or a second copy. Integrity comes from those pins, not from the server.

rollback.action: Stop the HTTP server and delete the serve directory.

procedures.title: Check that a surviving mirror serves reads

steps.action: Probe the mirror's relay role.
steps.expect: Exit 0 (pass) or 3 (degraded). Exit 4 means nothing answered: treat it as loss, never as an empty repository.

verify.check: The probe verdict is pass or degraded.

rollback.action: Nothing to undo: the probe sends only reads.

procedures.title: Accept pushes and pull requests without the hosted service

steps.action: Check the node before starting it.
Start the node with the hosted tunnel disabled and your own endpoints.
steps.unsafe: Leaving --upstream at its default points the node at forkmesh.com, which is unavailable.

verify.check: The relay role probe passes against the node.

rollback.action: Stop the node. Submissions it spooled but did not commit are kept in its pull submission spool.

procedures.title: Clone over the local network with no DNS

steps.action: Write a lan-only transport profile from the roster's pinned addresses.
Confirm the mirror's route uses a pinned address and needs no DNS.
Clone over that route. On Linux the Git process is traced for DNS queries and off-route connections.
steps.expect: Exit 0. Exit 5 means a DNS query or off-route connection was seen.

verify.check: The transport exits 0, not 4 (unreachable) or 5 (exposed).
The clone's refs match a signed export or a second copy.

rollback.action: Delete the clone and the profile.

steps.action: Export a signed copy to the media.
On the receiving side, verify the media against the pinned export key.
Import it. Diverged refs are kept aside, never overwritten.
steps.unsafe: Never pass --allow-unpinned during an incident: anyone can sign media.

verify.check: Import exits 0, or 5 with conflicts kept aside for review.

procedures.title: Replace a lost or stolen signing key

steps.action: Generate the successor key on a machine that verified the kit.
The first custodian writes and signs the rotation statement.
steps.unsafe: The lost key must never sign its own replacement, and the threshold must never be lowered during an incident.

steps.action: Each further custodian checks the keys against paper and adds a signature until the threshold is met.
Apply the rotation to write the new roster.
For a mirror node identity, import the node's sealed identity export instead.

verify.check: key apply exits 0 and roster check lists the lost key as revoked.
Media signed by the revoked key now fails import, and media signed by the successor imports.

rollback.action: A rotation cannot be unsigned. Keep the old roster file for the record, and issue a further rotation if the successor was wrong.

procedures.title: Restore from the newest backup that verifies

steps.action: Verify copies newest first. Stop at the first that verifies.
steps.unsafe: Never import a copy that failed verification, and never repair a bundle by hand.

steps.action: Import the verified copy into an empty repository.

verify.check: Connectivity check passes.
The scribe records which newer copies were rejected, and which commits they held that are now lost.

rollback.action: Delete the restored repository; the backups were only read.

procedures.title: Restore a mirror node from its encrypted backup

steps.action: Rehearse the archive in scratch space first.
Dry-run, then restore onto the new host.
Restore for real.
steps.unsafe: Never run the old host and its restored copy at the same time.

verify.check: Preflight reports no errors.

rollback.action: A failed restore deletes everything it created. Try the next older archive.

steps.action: Each region exports with its own key, and the media travels both ways.
Each region imports the other's media. Diverged branches are kept under refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/.
steps.unsafe: Never force-push a region's branch over the other's kept-aside work.

steps.action: Review each kept-aside branch and merge it through a normal pull request.

verify.check: Every commit from both regions is reachable in both repositories.

steps.action: Compare the returning service's refs with the restored network before anything syncs.
Push restored work to the returning service as fast-forwards only.
steps.unsafe: Never let the returning service overwrite work done during the incident.

steps.action: Stop emergency static mirrors and temporary profiles.
Rebuild and re-sign the bootstrap kit with the current roster.
Write the exercise or incident record with a corrective owner for every finding.

verify.check: The new kit verifies against the kit key on paper.

rollback.action: Keep serving from the restored network, and try the return again later.

kit.question: Has the bootstrap kit verified against the kit key written on paper?

kit-ok.question: Did the kit verify (exit 0, or exit 4 stale)?

stop-kit.text: Stop. Do not run tools from unverified media. Get the second custodian's kit and the printed runbook.

keys.question: Is a signing key, recovery key, or passphrase lost or possibly stolen?

backup.question: Did a backup or export fail to verify?

names.question: Do hostnames fail to resolve while addresses still answer?

isolated.question: Is your region cut off from every other region?

origin.question: Is a repository's origin host gone or wiped?

service.question: Are hosted services (website, index, sign-in, collaboration inboxes) unavailable?

newcomer.question: Does a new member or machine need to join with no internet?

no-incident.text: No scenario applies. Record what you saw and keep watching.

scenarios.title: Origin loss
signals: The origin host is gone, wiped, or refuses every read.
Mirrors still hold copies, possibly a little behind.

copy.question: Does at least one surviving copy verify against a signed export or a second copy?

media.question: Is there a verified removable-media export?

done.text: The new origin is verified and serving.

lost.text: No verified copy survives. Ask every roster contact for clones, and follow crisis preservation for public copies elsewhere.

scenarios.title: Main-service loss
signals: forkmesh.com, its sign-in, index, or collaboration inboxes do not answer.

reachable.question: Does a roster mirror answer reads?

writes.question: Must the community accept pushes and pull requests before service returns?

done.text: The community reads, and if needed writes, without the hosted service.

scenarios.title: DNS loss
signals: Hostnames do not resolve, or resolve to the wrong place.
Addresses on the roster still answer.

address.question: Does the roster list an address or pinned host for a mirror you can reach?

clean.question: Did the transport exit 0 (not unreachable or exposed)?

others.question: Do other people on the network need the repository?

done.text: Repositories move by address or media, with no DNS.

scenarios.title: Key loss
signals: A signing key, device, or passphrase is lost.
A key may be in someone else's hands.

threshold.question: Can the roster's threshold of recovery key custodians sign?

wait.text: Do not lower the threshold. Treat media signed by the lost key as untrusted and wait for custodians.

check.question: Is media signed by the revoked key refused, and media signed by the successor imported?

done.text: The successor key is trusted and the lost key is revoked.

scenarios.title: Regional isolation
signals: A region has no connection to other regions, while its local network still works.

holder.question: Does anyone in your region hold a mirror or clone?

carry.question: Can someone carry media between regions?

local.text: Keep working locally, export on a schedule, and carry media when a route opens.

reconnected.question: Has the network between regions returned?

exchanging.text: Regions stay in step by carried media until the network returns.

done.text: Both regions hold every commit, and diverged work is under review.

scenarios.title: Corrupted backup
signals: A backup or export fails verification.
A restore drill fails its checks.

kind.question: Is the failing backup a mirror node archive (.fmbackup)?

none.text: No copy verifies. Do not repair bundles by hand; ask roster contacts for clones.

newer.question: Does a mirror or clone hold commits newer than the restored copy?

done.text: Restored from the newest verified copy; losses are recorded.

scenarios.title: Offline bootstrap
signals: A new member or machine must join with no internet.
The only material is the printed runbook, the kit, and keys on paper.

stop.text: Do not run anything from the kit. Get the second custodian's kit.

done.text: The new member holds a verified clone and the verified kit.
